local_validation.change_scope: Only the new, not-yet-native-tested GPU queue kernels change after full make check: each token compacts into a bounded shared2048-entry queue and publishes one global allocation per pass instead of one allocation per wave. The host owner, mock and native fixture remain byte-identical. Native validation must exercise final source.

spec.model: none; generated BF16 operand component or native compile
spec.purpose: Build and compare fused and global-queue actual linear OUT adaptive replay. The new route packs BF16 interval endpoints into the existing F32 matrix storage and executes original K16 dots in independent global grid-stride kernels. At most18 GPU queue resets/replay/certificate rounds use no host count reads; final statistics remain host-validated. The63 generated cases additionally check queue/state/cost redzones and the restored rounded F32 carrier. A four-CTA numerical grid forces multiple replay iterations; the product owner uses4096 CTAs. Both variants are compared against independent CPU original dots and the full unchanged residual RMSNorm consumer. The original K16 carry arithmetic replays selected values; certification covers original unrounded residual variance, rsqrt lookup and every normalized BF16 endpoint. Up to18 rounds finish all original selected cells on failed certification. Generated numerical cases use independent CPU original dots followed by the unchanged GPU residual/normalization consumer. Inputs, prepared rows, statistics and consumer redzones are checked. A deliberately invalid producer envelope must trigger observed-boundary fallback. No real-model or performance acceptance is inherited from these components.

scope: Default-off variant2 separates original K16 replay from per-token certificate arrays and shared barriers. A bounded2048-entry token queue publishes one global allocation per pass. Packed BF16 interval endpoints reuse the original F32 matrix storage; exact replays write BF16 output and the final conversion restores its rounded F32 carrier. At most18 rounds reset and consume GPU counts with no host count read. The host owner, failure injection and63 generated cases exercise both fused and queued variants. Each case compares the complete unchanged GPU residual/normalization consumer and all queue/state/cost/output redzones. Final source differs from the full local check only in the previously unexecuted GPU queue compaction; subsequent local owner/C/hygiene checks and these Windows runs cover the final source. Generated component centers are based on independent original CPU dot endpoints, including deliberately selected midpoints; this checks kernel and consumer behavior, not the accuracy of the matrix producer envelope for arbitrary data. The unchanged original GPU residual/normalization consumer compares all residual and normalized F32/BF16 bits against independent CPU original updates. Nonfinite normalization forces bounded full replay; deliberately invalid centers require observed-boundary failure and complete original selected replay. The certificate depends on the existing empirical producer PPB/midpoint envelope. An observed violation disables certification and finishes all selected cells, but unobserved interval undercoverage is not proven impossible. Real-model GB10 gates and product timing remain separate. Host fault injection checks the real allocation/transport/drain owner, not GPU arithmetic.
